meta.question: Why did checkout fail for 47 minutes on 14/10/2026, and what are we changing?
meta.title: Incident review: checkout outage, 14/10/2026
meta.author: Platform on-call
meta.footer: Blameless review. Internal; do not forward outside the company.

answer.headline: An expired TLS certificate on the payment gateway's internal endpoint made every card payment fail; renewal had silently stopped because the job's service account lost access during a permissions clean-up.
answer.text: Orders were accepted but payments were rejected, so customers saw a generic error at the last step. No card was charged twice and no data was lost.
points: Root cause: certificate renewal job lost its permissions on 12/09/2026
Detection took 11 minutes because the error-rate alert waits for 10 minutes of failures
Five follow-up actions; two are already done

items.title: Service account permissions tidied up
items.text: A clean-up removed the renewal job's write access to the certificate store. The job began failing quietly.

items.title: Certificate expires
items.text: Calls from the order service to the payment gateway fail the TLS handshake.

items.title: Alert fires
items.text: The checkout error-rate alert pages the on-call engineer.

items.title: Cause found
items.text: Gateway logs show `certificate has expired` on every request.

items.title: Service restored
items.text: A certificate was issued by hand and the gateway reloaded. Error rate back to normal.

blocks.title: Why the renewal failure went unnoticed
blocks.label: Silent failure
blocks.body: The renewal job logged its errors but nothing alerted on them, and the certificate had 30 days of validity left when it first failed. **A job that fails safely for a month still needs an alert.**

items.text: Restore the renewal job's permissions and renew all gateway certificates
Alert when any certificate has fewer than 14 days left
Alert on renewal job failures, not only on expiry
Show a clear retry message when payment is unavailable
Review service accounts before removing permissions

items.q: Were any customers charged without an order?
items.a: No. Payments failed before authorisation, so no money moved. Finance confirmed this against the provider's settlement report.

items.q: Why did it take 18 minutes to find the cause after the alert?
items.a: The first responder looked at the recent deploy, which was unrelated. The gateway's TLS errors were only in its own logs, not on the checkout dashboard.

items.q: Could this happen to other services?
items.a: Yes, any service using the same renewal job. The expiry alert now covers all 23 certificates in the store.

answer.headline: The renewal job lost write access to the certificate store during a permissions clean-up on 12/09/2026, and every run after that failed quietly.
points: The job ran every night and logged its failure at debug level only
Nothing checked when the certificate would expire

items.title: Permissions clean-up
items.text: Unused service-account roles were removed, including the renewal job's write role.

items.title: Nightly runs fail
items.text: The job could not write the new certificate, logged it at debug level and exited without an error code.

items.title: Certificate expires
items.text: The gateway kept serving the old certificate until it expired, and every card payment failed.

blocks.title: Why nobody was paged
blocks.body: The failure looked like a slow rise in errors, and the error-rate alert waits 10 minutes before it fires.

answer.headline: The error-rate alert fires only after 10 minutes above its threshold, to avoid paging on short spikes; a sudden total failure should page at once.
points: Add a second rule: 100% failures for 1 minute pages immediately
Alert 14 days before any certificate expires
